newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar in copper-foil pact with Japan firms.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar in copper-foil pact with Japan firms.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said on Monday it would form a T$2.25 billion (US$81.81 million) joint venture on September 13 with three Japanese firms to make copper foil in Taiwan.
"This venture will help to supply Taiwan's high-technology industries," a Taiwan Sugar manager told Reuters.
Taiwan Sugar would hold 45 percent of the venture with over T$1 billion (US$36.36 million) in capital investment, she said.

Japan's Furukawa Electric Co, Nichimen Corp and Furukawa Circuit Foil would hold 55 percent, she said without disclosing each Japanese firm's stake. Furukawa Circuit Foil is a subsidiary of Furukawa Electric Co.
A signing ceremony would be held on September 13 and further details would be made public then, the spokeswoman said.
The foil plant to be built at Touliu in southern Taiwan will be compeleted by December 1998, she added.
Demand for copper foil has been growing as it is a key manufacturing material in computers and mobile telephones.

Taiwan Sugar, whose sugar monopoly in Taiwan ends in 2002, has already begun branching out into new investments including real estate, construction and farming, exploiting its large land holdings. (Conversion: $1=T$27.5) -- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
